description.p: Arkha is a fast file manager for Linux, modelled on Caja (MATE). It uses your desktop’s GTK theme, icons and bookmarks, and feels at home on MATE, but works on any desktop.

ul.li: Icon, list, compact and columns views
Split view with two panes, each with its own tabs
Tabs like a browser: reopen closed tabs, drag them between windows
An info panel with a folder’s cover picture or a file’s preview
Rename many files at once: change case, insert, remove, replace, number
Undo and redo of file operations, and copies checked against their originals
Checksums (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, CRC32 and more) in a file’s properties
Your own context menu entries and thumbnailers, and every keyboard shortcut changeable

description.p: Arkha’s code was written by an AI, Anthropic’s Claude, directed and tested by its maintainer.

description.p: Search with or without subfolders, KDE's Ark, more choices for split view and tabs, and big folders that stay smooth:

ul.li: The search can include the folders inside the one searched, or look only in the folder itself; Preferences set how a new search starts.
Files dragged out of KDE's Ark are extracted where they're dropped, on X11 and Wayland. Extract Here and Compress can use Ark, and Preferences choose the archive manager.
Closing split view can keep either pane, and the extra pane and new tabs can open in the same folder, the home folder, the last one closed, or a folder of one's own.
A folder or search with more than 20,000 items is shown as a list instead of icons, and many items arriving at once or tabs not shown no longer freeze the window.
Thumbnails of files on network places, and of files dragged out of the Trash, go with their files.
Extract Here knows more archive types, the manual opens in the web browser, and arkha --version prints the version.

description.p: A manual, and Properties that follow what you drop on them:

ul.li: Help, Manual (F1) opens Arkha's manual in the web browser: what Arkha can do and where to find it, in English and German, installed with Arkha and read offline. If it's missing from the package, this version's manual can be read online.
A file or folder dragged into an open Properties window is shown in it, on the tab chosen before; a note still being typed is saved first.
The messages about files too big for FAT32 drives are translated into German.

description.p: Safer, with thumbnails that keep up with your files:

ul.li: Thumbnailers run in a sandbox (with bubblewrap installed): a file made to exploit one can't reach your files.
Thumbnails move with files moved or renamed in Arkha, go when files are deleted or the trash is emptied, and are made again for files whose first try failed while they were still arriving.

Custom actions with "%f" in quotes are safe from file names with commands in them; files dragged in from other programs neither replace nor hide anything; Enter in the "run or display" question no longer runs the file.
Files copied to USB sticks and drives formatted for Windows get names those can hold, and a file too big for FAT32 is said to be at once.
Search results follow files moved, trashed or deleted, and files cut from them paste with Ctrl+V in another tab.
File operations can be shown in their own window instead of the popup (Preferences, Behavior), and the popup stays open while a queued job takes over.
Rename All keeps notes, emblems and custom icons; a settings file with a faulty line no longer resets all settings; remembered folder views follow their folders.
About has buttons for the license and the source code.

description.p: Folders with many files open a little faster: their dates no longer look up the time zone once for each file.
The File Operations window, when open, stays open while a queued copy or move starts, until the last one is done.
The prebuilt program for other distributions now includes the German translation, which the one of 1.0.0 was missing.
